title: Joint Statement by the United States and the Baltic Countries following the 2026 Baltic 3+1 Energy Dialogue

documents.text:
Joint Statement by the United States and the Baltic Countries following the 2026 Baltic 3+1
                                       Energy Dialogue
                                      November 19, 2026

On November 19, 2026, representatives of the Ministries of Energy for the three Baltic countries
of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania and the United States Secretary of Energy convened for the
sixth 3+1 Energy Dialogue on the margins of the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy
Cooperation (P-TEC) Ministerial in Warsaw, Poland. Estonia’s Vice Minister of Energy and
Mineral Resources Jaanus Uiga, Latvia’s State Secretary of Climate and Energy Līga Kurevska,
Lithuania’s Minister of Energy Lukas Savickas, and U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright
affirmed their shared commitment to strengthening their strategic energy partnership—ensuring
access to affordable and reliable energy; enhancing the security and resilience of critical energy
infrastructure; expanding the import of U.S. liquified natural gas (LNG) to continue diversifying
European energy supplies; and advancing the deployment of innovative civil nuclear
technologies.

The representatives and Secretary recognized the longstanding and successful energy
cooperation between the United States, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, including U.S. technical
assistance that contributed to the historic separation of the Baltic electricity grid from Russia and
its subsequent synchronization with the Central European grid in February 2025. Building on
this milestone, they determined to continue technical cooperation to bolster energy security, grid
resilience, and system reliability.

The representatives and Secretary discussed persistent physical and cyber threats to the Baltic
energy system, including risks to undersea and aboveground electric grid infrastructure, natural
gas and liquid fuel supplies, and energy distribution. Recognizing the security of critical energy
infrastructure as a shared strategic priority, they emphasized the importance of continued
cooperation to enhance infrastructure protection, preparedness, and resilience against potential
disruptions.

The representatives and Secretary emphasized that access to affordable, reliable, and secure
electricity is essential to economic competitiveness, industrial growth, and national security.
They highlighted the importance of transparent and fair electricity markets in reducing costs,
encouraging investment, and supporting efficient electricity generation, as well as the role of
stronger regional electricity interconnections in enhancing grid reliability, energy security, and
market integration. They further emphasized the importance of avoiding premature retirement of
reliable generating assets where doing so could undermine grid reliability, increase electricity
costs, or compromise energy security.

The representatives and Secretary discussed Europe’s steps and strategies to reduce energy
dependence on adversaries in 2027, and the United States expressed its readiness to expand LNG
supplies to the Baltic region, while the Baltic countries continue efforts to increase LNG import
capacity and diversify regional energy supplies.
 The assessment of innovative civil nuclear technologies, including small modular reactors, and
the exploration of their potential deployment remain areas of cooperation among the four
countries. Such technologies could contribute to reliable electricity generation, enhance the
resilience of the Baltic power grid, and strengthen long-term energy security. The representatives
and the Secretary recognized the potential role of U.S. civil nuclear technologies in the Baltic
region and determined to continue cooperation on technology, nuclear safety, regulatory
frameworks, knowledge sharing, and the assessment of potential economic viability, taking into
account national decision-making processes and the needs of each country’s energy system.

The representatives and Secretary underscored their countries’ continued support for Ukraine
and its people. The United States’ passage of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and
Iran Act of 2026 and the €90 billion Ukrainian support loan package by the European Union are
important contributions to bringing a just and lasting peace closer in Ukraine.

The Baltic countries and the United States value the Baltic 3+1 Energy Dialogue for advancing
shared energy security priorities and future-oriented transatlantic cooperation. Looking ahead,
they reaffirmed their commitment to a strong transatlantic partnership grounded in trust, mutual
interests, and shared vision for a secure, resilient, and prosperous future. Through continued
engagement under the 3+1 Energy Dialogue, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and the United States
aim to enhance energy security, foster innovation, and deepen their strategic energy partnership
to help build a more secure, resilient, and prosperous future.
